practices.practice: When using DocumentDB's integrated vector features, create and query vector indexes with the `cosmosSearch` operator (vector-diskann / vector-hnsw / vector-ivf) and tune index parameters such as dimensions, similarity (COS/L2/IP), lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree/efConstruction to match dataset size and recall/latency targets.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector search DiskANN HNSW IVF cosmosSearch createSearchIndexes

practices.practice: Normalize embeddings at ingestion (L2 / unit-length) when you use cosine similarity, and store the embedding model name, dimensions, and a version in the document so you can detect model drift and reindex safely.
practices.prior_belief: Normalize embeddings consistently (e.g., L2-normalize) if you intend to use cosine similarity so index distance metric and scoring match how embeddings are compared at query time.
practices.how_found: documentdb-vector-search (vector-normalize-embeddings.md)

practices.practice: Store embeddings as numeric arrays on a dedicated field (e.g., embedding: number[]) and create a vector index for that field (one vector index per path) rather than indexing embeddings as text.
practices.prior_belief: Store embeddings as float32 arrays in a dedicated field (e.g., embedding) and avoid indexing them as text; create a vector index specifically for that field (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) with parameters tuned to embedding dimensionality and recall/latency tradeoffs.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector search DiskANN HNSW IVF cosmosSearch createSearchIndexes

practices.practice: When building RAG, chunk long documents before embedding and vectorizing; use token-aware chunking (start around 512 tokens ≈ 2000 characters) with overlap (e.g., ~25%) and record chunk metadata (parent_id/product_id, chunk_id, source, token_count) to enable selective retrieval and prompt-budgeting.
practices.prior_belief: When ingesting long product documents, chunk them into 200–500 token segments, compute embeddings per chunk, and store chunk metadata (product_id, chunk_id, token_count, source) to enable retrieval, reranking, and prompt construction.
practices.source_name: Chunk large documents for RAG and vector search in Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector search chunking RAG 'chunk large documents' guidance

practices.practice: At query time, request a top-k (e.g., k=5) vector result set from the vector index and then apply metadata filters and a lightweight reranker or token-budget-aware trimming (using stored token_count) to select which chunks to include in the LLM prompt.
practices.prior_belief: During vector search retrieval, fetch the top-N (e.g., 5) candidate chunks by vector score and then run a small text-based reranker or heuristic filter using metadata and token budgets before constructing the LLM prompt.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector search 'k' 'top k' 'rerank' 'cosmosSearch'

practices.practice: Choose vector index type by scale: use vector-ivf for small datasets, vector-hnsw up to moderate scale (tens of thousands), and prefer DiskANN for high-scale production workloads (hundreds of thousands+); tune nlist/M/efConstruction/lBuild/lSearch and consider product quantization or fp16 for high-dimensional vectors.
practices.prior_belief: Tune vector index parameters (e.g., M and efConstruction for HNSW or nlist for IVF) according to embedding dimension and target recall/latency, and validate with a representative recall/latency benchmark set.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index tuning DiskANN HNSW IVF

practices.practice: Prefer DocumentDB-native full-text search: create search indexes with `createSearchIndexes` and query with the `$search` aggregation stage (BM25, fuzzy, phrase, custom analyzers) rather than relying on MongoDB `$text` indexes.
practices.how_found: documentdb-indexing (index-text-prefer-textsearch.md)

practices.practice: Hybrid retrieval (BM25 text search + vector search) is supported and recommended for some scenarios: build search indexes via `createSearchIndexes`, use `$search` for BM25 results and combine or fuse BM25 and vector rankings (e.g., Reciprocal Rank Fusion) rather than forbidding coexisting lexical and vector indexes.
practices.prior_belief: Keep the embedding vector field out of text indexes and do not create both a full-text index and a vector index on the same field; vector indexes should be declared via the cluster’s vector indexing APIs/settings.
practices.how_found: documentdb-full-text-search (fts-hybrid-search.md)

practices.practice: Create single-field or compound indexes for frequently-filtered metadata (product_id, locale, language, created_at) so you can pre-filter before vector search and avoid scanning the whole collection.
practices.prior_belief: Create secondary (non-vector) indexes on frequently filtered metadata fields (e.g., product_id, locale, language, created_at) to make pre-filtering before vector search efficient.
practices.how_found: documentdb-indexing (index-pattern-cookbook.md)

practices.practice: Limit returned fields at query time (use projection) to only the data needed for prompt construction (text, metadata, product_id) to reduce network transfer and serialization cost.
practices.prior_belief: Limit returned document fields using projection to only the fields needed for the prompt (text, product_id, metadata) to reduce network transfer and serialization cost during retrieval.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Node.js
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB projection reduce network transfer 'projection' 'project'

practices.practice: Use a single MongoClient per process (singleton) and reuse it across requests; in serverless environments initialize the client outside the function handler to enable connection reuse and avoid pool exhaustion.
practices.prior_belief: Use connection pooling with a tuned maxPoolSize and socketTimeoutMS matching your concurrency needs; avoid creating one client per request — reuse a shared client/process-wide pool.
practices.how_found: documentdb-connection (singleton client pattern and serverless guidance)

practices.practice: Tune pooling parameters by environment: serverless functions use small pools (maxPoolSize 3–5, minPoolSize 0, short maxIdleTimeMS), long-running servers use larger pools pre-warmed to expected concurrency.
practices.how_found: documentdb-connection (serverless vs OLTP pool tuning)

practices.practice: Implement retries for transient errors with exponential backoff and jitter and honor server-provided retry signals (e.g., 429 Retry-After) rather than immediate aggressive retries.
practices.prior_belief: Implement exponential backoff with jitter and honor server-provided Retry-After headers for transient failures and 429 rate-limited responses rather than aggressive immediate retries.
practices.how_found: documentdb-connection (retry logic example and 429 handling)

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logging and alert on cluster metrics (CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, connection saturation) and use explain()/indexStats to detect full-collection scans and confirm index usage.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and monitor query latencies, index build times, memory and disk usage, and rate-limited (429) occurrences; use explain() and the MCP/documentdb tools to validate that queries are using the intended vector/index.
practices.how_found: documentdb-monitoring (monitoring-slow-query-log & metrics alerts)

practices.practice: Choose shard key only after evaluating workload: prefer single-shard unless size/throughput requires sharding; read-heavy workloads should pick a key that localizes frequent filters, write-heavy should pick a high-cardinality evenly-distributed key and avoid monotonic or skewed keys.
practices.prior_belief: Choose a partition key that evenly distributes writes and reads (e.g., hashed product_id or product_category depending on access patterns) and avoid high-cardinality hot keys; test performance with realistic traffic.
practices.how_found: documentdb-sharding (sharding-shard-key-selection.md)

practices.practice: Keep the number of secondary indexes modest (typical guidance 5–15 per collection) and use index lifecycle: inventory → hideIndex → test → dropIndex to safely remove unused indexes.
practices.how_found: documentdb-indexing (index-count-budget.md, index-lifecycle-drop-hide.md)

practices.practice: Use explain('executionStats') and the MCP/documentdb tools to validate query plans and confirm that vector and metadata filters are being applied and not causing full-collection scans.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain plans and indexStats to confirm that vector/metadata filters are applied and to detect full-collection scans; after creating indexes, re-run ingestion or compacting steps if required by the cluster to make indexes active.
practices.how_found: documentdb-query-optimization (use explain to verify index usage)

practices.practice: Use field-level or customer-managed encryption and avoid storing unnecessary PII in embeddings or chunk text; prefer encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys for regulated workloads.
practices.prior_belief: Keep sensitive PII out of embeddings and stored chunk text when possible; if PII must be stored, use field-level encryption or server-side encryption with customer-managed keys.
practices.how_found: documentdb-security (security-cmk-encryption.md & security-private-endpoint.md)

practices.practice: Always require TLS for DocumentDB connections (ensure tls=true and SCRAM-SHA-256 in connection string) and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Always connect using TLS/SSL and verify the server certificate; configure the MongoDB driver to require TLS and reject unauthorized certificates in production.
practices.how_found: documentdb-connection (TLS is required, connection string examples)

practices.practice: Prefer managed identity / Microsoft Entra ID / RBAC or Key Vault references to long-lived connection credentials in production and never commit connection strings or secrets to source control; read connection strings from environment variables or secret stores at runtime.
practices.prior_belief: Read the connection string only from a runtime secret store or environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never hard-code, commit, or log the URI/credentials.
practices.source_name: Store application secrets safely during development / App Service connection strings
practices.how_found: Azure secrets guidance 'store connection string outside code' 'Key Vault references env var'

practices.practice: When embedding/ingesting many documents, design idempotent ingestion (upserts with stable idempotency keys), use optimistic retry-safe patterns, and include schemaVersion / embeddingVersion metadata so reindexing is possible after model changes.
practices.prior_belief: Version embeddings, schema, and indexes (store embedding model name + version in chunk metadata) so that when you upgrade the embedding model or change chunking you can reindex or filter old vectors safely.
practices.how_found: documentdb-vector-search (vector-normalize-embeddings.md) and RAG enrichment guidance

practices.practice: Use the MCP/documentdb toolset or SDKs to list collections and indexes, create vector and search indexes programmatically (createIndexes / createSearchIndexes or runCommand), and to retrieve searchScore (`$meta: "searchScore"`) when projecting $search results.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB (quickstarts)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB quickstart vector index examples createIndexes createSearchIndexes $meta searchScore

practices.practice: When ingesting many documents to DocumentDB, respect batch-write limits (DocumentDB documents are 16 MB max and batch writes have documented limits), and tune client-side batch sizes and parallelism to avoid exceeding per-request or per-thread write thresholds.
practices.source_name: Document size and batch write limits in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB document size and batch write limits '16 MB' 'max writes per batch'

practices.practice: For serverless functions initialize the MongoClient outside the handler and use small maxPoolSize/minPoolSize and short maxIdleTimeMS so warm instances reuse connections while minimizing idle connections.
practices.how_found: documentdb-connection (serverless pattern guidance)

practices.practice: Use explain() / `explain("executionStats")` to capture planner selection and executionStats after index creation and during migration workflows (create new index → hide old → test → drop) to avoid regressions.
practices.source_name: Migrate to ordered indexes in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB indexing migration 'explain executionStats' 'hideIndex' workflow

practices.practice: When building embedding/vector pipelines, prefer integrated vectorization or managed indexer pipelines (Content Understanding / indexers) when available to get consistent chunking, embedding, and metadata enrichment rather than ad-hoc client-side pipelines.

practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB/Foundry chunking integrated vectorization 'Content Understanding skill' 'indexProjections'

practices.practice: Store provenance and enrichment metadata (source, page/chunk index, embeddingModel, embeddingDims, embeddingVersion, token_count) for each chunk so retrieval, filtering, re-embedding and auditing are possible.
practices.source_name: RAG chunk enrichment phase / Prepare data for AI app

practices.practice: Use explain and the MCP/documentdb tools to list collections, view index definitions, and confirm that newly created vector or search indexes exist and are ready before relying on them in production queries.

practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB quickstart 'create index if not exists' 'list indexes' 'verify index ready'

practices.practice: Apply minimal tunings to client timeouts (connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS) appropriate to the workload: short for fail-fast server selection, longer for expected long-running analytical queries.
practices.how_found: documentdb-connection (timeout tuning guidance)

practices.practice: Prefer managed authentication options (managed identities / Microsoft Entra ID + RBAC) for production instead of embedding static database passwords in app code or environment where possible.
practices.how_found: documentdb-security (security-entra-rbac.md)
